principles.text: Don't rush to flip aggressively to the short side just because of a pullback; while the market is still in an uptrend, treat a selloff as a short-term correction of a longer-term move and prefer sitting out over fighting the trend.
Playing both long and short aggressively in an uptrend has burned him before (December and February drawdowns); avoid being too aggressive shorting in an uptrend.
Price is the best indicator (roughly 80% price, 20% volume); don't hunt for the 'best' EMA or indicator since all are derived from price and volume.
Extreme extension plus volume spikes on leaders (e.g. a mega-cap gapping up 30% on huge volume) is a warning sign that the move can't last, even if it pushes higher first.

On every pullback or correction, hunt for the next leaders — names holding up with relative strength vs the indices often become the biggest movers of the next leg (e.g. Marvell in March, QCOM-style late starters).
Once you make a decision (e.g. an exit rule), follow your plan; whether someone holds to 200 or sells below the 9 EMA matters less than committing to and following the plan.
He uses no fixed profit targets on shorts; covers some near the lows of the prior flush/pin-bar candles and trails the rest down based on price action.
